2608.11181.title: How to Verify Consistency of Probabilistic Claims
2608.11181.paper_summary: When a probabilistic predictor answers many conditional-probability queries, are its answers self-consistent, and can this be verified in polynomial time? This problem is of interest for AI safety, where safety is derived from honesty about probabilistic predictions of unwanted outcomes potentially caused by an AI action. We construct an interactive PCP as follows. Let a predictive model be specified by a probability circuit P and a circuit Q which outputs confidence in predictions. Together, P and Q implicitly specify exponentially many probabilistic claims. We show a protocol in which a polynomial-time verifier can verify the approximate consistency of (P,Q). The verifier is given the pair of circuits (P,Q), which it evaluates at only a few points; alongside them it is given a proof oracle, an encoding of a witnessing probability distribution allegedly consistent with the predictions of (P,Q), which it reads at a few locations while interacting with a single untrusted prover. En route, we must ensure the existence of a sparse witnessing distribution consistent with the model's predictions. To do so, we first consider witness distributions for the consistency of explicit probabilistic claims, rather than claims specified by a predictor: say m claims, each of the form Pr[Y = 1 | X = x] = p, over n Boolean variables. Building on work initiated by Nilsson (Artif. Intell., 1986), we place l_2-approximate probabilistic consistency of explicit claims in NP, with certificates of length O(mn + log B) in the input bit-precision B; we further show how a small additive completeness-soundness gap removes the dependence on B. Together these results provide a complexity-theoretic foundation for certifying the self-consistency of probabilistic predictors. We view our interactive PCP as a first step toward training predictive models to prove their own consistency.
2608.11181.paper_summary_zh: 當一個概率預測器回答許多條件概率查詢時，它的答案是否自洽，這是否可以在多項式時間內驗證？這個問題對於人工智慧安全性來說非常重要，安全性源於對可能由人工智慧行動引起的不良結果的概率預測的誠實性。我們構建了一個互動式的 PCP，如下所示。讓一個預測模型由概率電路 P 和輸出預測信心的電路 Q 來指定。P 和 Q 一起隱式地指定了指數多的概率聲明。我們展示了一個協議，其中多項式時間的驗證者可以驗證 (P,Q) 的近似一致性。驗證者獲得電路對 (P,Q)，它僅在少數幾個點上對其進行評估；同時，它獲得了一個證明預言機，一個編碼的見證概率分佈，據稱與 (P,Q) 的預測一致，它在與單個不可信的證明者互動時在幾個位置上讀取。途中，我們必須確保存在一個與模型預測一致的稀疏見證分佈。為此，我們首先考慮顯式概率聲明的一致性的見證分佈，而不是由預測器指定的聲明：假設 m 個聲明，每個形式為 Pr[Y = 1 | X = x] = p，涉及 n 個布爾變量。基於 Nilsson（Artif. Intell., 1986）所開展的工作，我們將顯式聲明的 l_2-近似概率一致性置於 NP 中，證明的長度為 O(mn + log B)，其中輸入位精度為 B；我們進一步展示如何通過小的加性完整性-健壯性差距來消除對 B 的依賴。這些結果共同為證明概率預測器的自洽性提供了一個複雜性理論基礎。我們將我們的互動式 PCP 視為訓練預測模型以證明其自身一致性的第一步。
